findings.finding: No test pins the reporting direction of the new prose-rule arm. Nothing asserts that, with a wired dataset, an interaction-rule partner the answer does NOT name by its drug is still appended as 'not named above' and still counted unstated. Every pre-existing appending/undercount case in CitedFindingPartnerCompletionTest builds its validator with DrugReferenceTestSupport.validatorRaising(null, chips) (line 621). namesThePartner returns false at its `drugReferenceService == null` guard, so those cases never reach the prose-rule arm and do not run the production configuration. The five new cases all assert the 'stated' direction. Add a case on the OverShippedData arrangement: the answer cites the Rifampicin finding without naming rifampicin, and the test asserts the appended sentence and findingPartners {2,1}.
findings.failure_mode: If namesThePartner stops consulting the prose (e.g. returns true on any row-id match), the module never appends an omitted order of an interaction-rule finding, and findingPartners.stated always equals named for them. In production every resolved interaction-rule partner carries rows, so ADR Decision 100's completion and the findingPartners diagnostic are switched off for the most common finding type. The suite stays green.
findings.evidence: Mutation: DrugSafetyValidator.namesThePartner `if (ids.contains(row.getId()) && namesAnyOf(lower, row))` changed to `if (ids.contains(row.getId()))`. CitedFindingPartnerCompletionTest (14 tests), FindingPartnerLogDisclosureTest (6) and LlmInferenceServiceAnswerFromFindingsContextTest (27) all pass with 0 failures (surefire reports). Unmutated, a throwaway probe on the alprazolam arrangement ('…active order Nevirapine [4] and with another of her orders [5].') returns the appended 'active order Rifampicin (rifampin)' and FindingPartnerCoverage{named=2, stated=1}. The production behaviour is right; it is just not pinned. File restored and git status clean.

findings.finding: Ticket coverage check, recorded for the next round: the ticket's second question ('Can I add dolutegravir to her regimen?') has no case of its own. It goes through the same drug-in-play arm and resolves under the PR: a throwaway probe on the shipped KB with Nevirapine and Rifampicin orders returned an answer naming 'active order Rifampicin' byte for byte, with FindingPartnerCoverage{named=1, stated=1}. All three ticket shapes (alprazolam, dolutegravir, medication screen) resolve. No change required. A dolutegravir case would pin the ticket's whole list cheaply, if wanted.
findings.evidence: Throwaway test probeDolutegravir in CitedFindingPartnerCompletionTest (since reverted): output 'Dolutegravir needs a dose change: it interacts with active order Rifampicin [5]. | FindingPartnerCoverage{named=1, stated=1}'.

notes: Approach: carrying the partner's resolved rows structurally and asking DrugReference.matchesText through namesThePartner mirrors the sibling namesTheFindingsSubject/namesTheEndedOrderDrug. It avoids re-resolving the printed label (#151) and a fourth name-matching rule (reference CLAUDE.md 'Matching a drug name'). It is the right shape and better than stripping the parenthetical.

Every SafetyWarning copy path (withMatchedOrderNames, withCurrentOrderDisplays, asStatedInTheAnswer, aboutSubstance, asAboutAnEndedOrder) carries partnerRows. The partnerRows keys match namedPartners at all three write sites: singletonList(partnerName) for both arms, and `partners` for the merged chip.
The changes to CitationGroundingVerifierTest, LlmInferenceServiceTest and OrderStopDateStatementTest only add the constructor's new null argument.
The condition-mediated finding's orders carry no rows and no case measures them. The ADR amendment states this; it is residue in the reporting direction.
